arxiv-2202-11372.title: Localizing Small Apples in Complex Apple Orchard Environments
arxiv-2202-11372.creator: Christian Wilms, Robert Johanson, Simone Frintrop
arxiv-2202-11372.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christian Wilms, Robert Johanson, Simone Frintrop. The localization of fruits is an essential first step in automated agricultural pipelines for yield estimation or fruit picking. One example of this is the localization of apples in images of entire apple trees. Since the apples are very small objects in such scenarios, we tackle this problem by adapting the object proposal generation system AttentionMask that focuses on small objects.

arxiv-2203-05620.title: KDSource, a tool for the generation of Monte Carlo particle sources using kernel density estimation Journal: Annals of Nuclear Energy
arxiv-2203-05620.creator: N. S. Schmidt, O. I. Abbate, Z. M. Prieto, J. I. Robledo, J. I. Márquez Damián, A. A. Márquez, J. Dawidowski
arxiv-2203-05620.description: Abstract Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations have clearly contributed to improve the design of nuclear systems. When performing in-beam or shielding simulations a complexity arises due to the fact that particles must be tracked to regions far from the original source or behind the shielding, often lacking sufficient statistics.

arxiv-2203-06052.title: Magnetic anisotropy energies and metal-insulator transitions in monolayers of α \alpha -RuCl 3 and OsCl 3 on graphene
arxiv-2203-06052.creator: P. H. Souza, D. P. de Andrade Deus, W. H. Brito, R. H. Miwa
arxiv-2203-06052.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by P. H. Souza, D. P. de Andrade Deus, W. H. Brito, R. H. Miwa. Transition metal thriclorides, with 4 ​ d 4d or 5 ​ d 5d electrons, are materials at the forefront of recent studies about the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and strong Coulomb interactions. Within our first-principles calculations (DFT+ U U +SOC) we study the effects of graphene on the electronic and magnetic properties of the monolayers of α \alpha -RuCl 3 and OsCl 3 .

arxiv-2212-14000.title: Braid Arrangement Bimonoids and the Toric Variety of the Permutohedron
arxiv-2212-14000.creator: William Norledge
arxiv-2212-14000.description: Abstract . We show that the toric variety of the permutohedron (=permutohedral space) has the structure of a cocommutative bimonoid in species, with multiplication/comultiplication given by embedding/projecting-onto boundary divisors. In terms of Losev-Manin’s description of permutohedral space as a moduli space, multiplication is concatenation of strings of Riemann spheres and comultiplication is forgetting marked points.

arxiv-2302-14701.title: The Contest Game for Crowdsourcing Reviews
arxiv-2302-14701.creator: Marios Mavronicolas, Paul G. Spirakis
arxiv-2302-14701.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marios Mavronicolas, Paul G. Spirakis. We consider a contest game modelling a contest where reviews for a proposal are crowdsourced from n n players . Player i i has a skill s i s_{i} , strategically chooses a quality q ∈ { 1 , 2 , … , Q } q\in\{1,2,\ldots,Q\} for her review and pays an effort 𝖿 q ≥ 0 {\sf f}_{q}\geq 0 , strictly increasing with q q .

arxiv-2401-15867.title: An Information Aggregation Operator
arxiv-2401-15867.creator: Heyang Gong
arxiv-2401-15867.description: Abstract This study explores a new mathematical operator, symbolized as ∪ + \mathbin{\vtop{\halign{#\cr$\cup$\cr\scalebox{0.9}{$+$}\cr}}} , for information aggregation, aimed at enhancing traditional methods by directly amalgamating probability distributions. This operator facilitates the combination of probability densities, contributing a nuanced approach to probabilistic analysis. We apply this operator to a personalized incentive scenario, illustrating its potential in a practical context.

arxiv-2402-12494.title: Enumerating m m -clusters using exceptional sequences
arxiv-2402-12494.creator: Kiyoshi Igusa
arxiv-2402-12494.description: Abstract . We give a bijection between ordered m m -clusters and (complete) m m -exceptional sequences, a concept that we introduce for this purpose. This holds for all hereditary artin algebras. This extends the bijection in the m = 1 m=1 case shown in [ 13 ] .

arxiv-2503-03193.title: Saturation of 0-1 Matrices
arxiv-2503-03193.creator: Andrew Brahms, Alan Duan, Jesse Geneson, Jacob Greene
arxiv-2503-03193.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew Brahms, Alan Duan, Jesse Geneson, Jacob Greene. A 0-1 matrix M M contains a 0-1 matrix P P if M M has a submatrix P ′ P^{\prime} which can be turned into P P by changing some of the ones to zeroes. Matrix M M is P P - saturated if M M does not contain P P , but any matrix M ′ M^{\prime} derived from M M by changing a zero to a one must contain P P .

arxiv-2509-09683.title: Forecasting Clicks in Digital Advertising: Multimodal Inputs and Interpretable Outputs
arxiv-2509-09683.creator: Briti Gangopadhyay, Zhao Wang, Shingo Takamatsu
arxiv-2509-09683.description: Abstract . Forecasting click volume is a key task in digital advertising, influencing both revenue and campaign strategy. Traditional time series models rely solely on numerical data, often overlooking rich contextual information embedded in textual elements, such as keyword updates.

arxiv-2601-22805.title: SOMBRERO: Measuring and Steering Boundary Placement in End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Models
arxiv-2601-22805.creator: Pit Neitemeier, Alessio Serra, Jiaze Li, Sascha Wirges, Lukas Balles, Jan Hendrik Metzen
arxiv-2601-22805.description: Abstract Hierarchical sequence models replace fixed tokenization with learned segmentations that compress long byte sequences for efficient autoregressive modeling. While recent end-to-end methods can learn meaningful boundaries from the language-modeling objective alone, it remains difficult to quantitatively assess and systematically steer where compute is spent.

europmc-pmc8786632.creator: Su Y, Yuan D, Chen DG, Ng RH, Wang K, Choi J, Li S, Hong S, Zhang R, Xie J, Kornilov SA, Scherler K, Pavlovitch-Bedzyk AJ, Dong S, Lausted C, Lee I, Fallen S, Dai CL, Baloni P, Smith B, Duvvuri VR, Anderson KG, Li J, Yang F, Duncombe CJ, McCulloch DJ, Rostomily C, Troisch P, Zhou J, Mackay S, DeGottardi Q, May DH, Taniguchi R, Gittelman RM, Klinger M, Snyder TM, Roper R, Wojciechowska G, Murray K, Edmark R, Evans S, Jones L, Zhou Y, Rowen L, Liu R, Chour W, Algren HA, Berrington WR, Wallick JA, Cochran RA, Micikas ME, ISB-Swedish COVID-19 Biobanking Unit, Wrin T, Petropoulos CJ, Cole HR, Fischer TD, Wei W, Hoon DSB, Price ND, Subramanian N, Hill JA, Hadlock J, Magis AT, Ribas A, Lanier LL, Boyd SD, Bluestone JA, Chu H, Hood L, Gottardo R, Greenberg PD, Davis MM, Goldman JD, Heath JR.

However, quantifiable risk factors for PASC and their biological associations are poorly resolved. We executed a deep multi-omic, longitudinal investigation of 309 COVID-19 patients from initial...

plos-pone-0001261.creator: Silke von Ahlfen, Andreas Missel, Klaus Bendrat et al.

However, current data on adverse effects of standard pathological prac

plos-pone-0008275.description: PLOS ONE research article. Combination antiretroviral treatment (cART) has been very successful, especially among selected patients in clinical trials. The aim of this study was to describe outcomes of cART on the population level in a large national cohort. Characteristics of participants of the Swiss HIV

pmc-10567785.title: Stroke metrics during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic, a tale of two comprehensive stroke centers
pmc-10567785.creator: Lara Carvalho de Oliveira, Ana Ponciano, Nima Kashani, Suzete N F Guarda, Michael D Hill, Eric E Smith, Jillian M Stang, Anand Viswanathan, Ashby C Turner, Aravind Ganesh
pmc-10567785.description: Although a decrease in stroke admissions during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic has been observed, detailed analyses of the evolution of stroke metrics during the pandemic are lacking. We analyzed changes in stroke presentation, in-hospital systems-of-care, and treatment time metrics at two representative Comprehensive Stroke Centers (CSCs) during the first year of Coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic.

pmc-10692018.title: Correction: Exploring DrugCentral: from molecular structures to clinical effects
pmc-10692018.creator: Liliana Halip, Sorin Avram, Ramona Curpan, Ana Borota, Alina Bora, Cristian Bologa, Tudor I Oprea
pmc-10692018.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). rea was originally published Online First without Open Access. After publication in volume 37, issue 12, page 681–694 the author decided to opt for Open Choice and to make the article an Open Access publication.

pmc-11397789.title: A Review of the Establishment of Effective Conductive Pathways of Conductive Polymer Composites and Advances in Electromagnetic Shielding
pmc-11397789.creator: Xiaotian Nan, Yi Zhang, Jiahao Shen, Ruimiao Liang, Jiayi Wang, Lan Jia, Xiaojiong Yang, Wenwen Yu, Zhiyi Zhang
pmc-11397789.description: The enhancement of the electromagnetic interference shielding efficiency (EMI SE) for conductive polymer composites (CPCs) has garnered increasing attention. The shielding performance is influenced by conductivity, which is dependent on the establishment of effective conductive pathways. In this review, Schelkunoff’s theory on outlining the mechanism of electromagnetic interference shielding was briefly described.

pmc-11413050.title: Investigate-Design-Practice-Reflect: An Iterative Community-Engaged Action Process to Improve Population Health
pmc-11413050.creator: Marisa S Rosen, Ann E Rogers, Mary J Von Seggern, Brandon L Grimm, Athena K Ramos, Michaela A Schenkelberg, Regina E Idoate, David A Dzewaltowski
pmc-11413050.description: BackgroundCommunity-based coalitions are a common strategy for community engagement efforts targeting the improvement of a variety of population health outcomes. The typical processes that coalitions follow to organize efforts include steps that are sequential, slow, and time intensive. These processes also limit local decision-making to the selection of evidence-based policies or programs.

pmc-11480469.title: Evaluation of the influence of freeze–thaw cycles on the joint strength of granite in the Eastern Tibetan Plateau, China
pmc-11480469.creator: Lirong Qi, Jiading Wang, Dengfei Zhang, Yongshuang Zhang, Jianfei Ma
pmc-11480469.description: The freeze–thaw cycles will lead to rock deterioration and pose a significant threat to engineering stability in cold regions. In this study, granite samples collected from the Luanshibao Landslide in the Eastern Tibetan Plateau were subjected to a maximum of 120 freeze–thaw cycles at two temperature paths (− 10–20 °C and − 20–20 °C).

pmc-11710065.title: The participation of activating transcription factor 6 alpha, ATF6α, in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11710065.creator: Mariana Gomes Chauvet, Alinny Rosendo Isaac, Mychael V Lourenco
pmc-11710065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia in elderly humans worldwide. More than 40 million people currently suffer from AD, and this prevalence tends to increase considerably in the coming decades due to increased longevity. The unfolded protein response (UPR) is an adaptive signaling mechanism that aims to maintain cell viability under misfolded protein accumulation and endoplasmic reticulum stress. UPR activation is associated with neurodegenerative diseases, such as AD, leading to synaptic loss and neuronal death.

pmc-12532891.title: A novel prognostic nomogram for elderly patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
pmc-12532891.creator: Zhongwei Zhang, Xue Hu, Qunqun Jiang, Qian Du, Qianhui Chen, Xiaoping Chen, Mingqi Luo, Miao Tan, Liping Deng, Yong Xiong
pmc-12532891.description: BackgroundSevere fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a life-threatening infectious disease triggered by a novel bunyavirus (SFTSV). The elderly population is vulnerable to infectious diseases. This study aimed to explore the clinical features and outcomes of elderly patients with SFTS and establish an effective prognostic nomogram for them.

pmc-12671495.title: Mapping light-harvesting and photoprotection responses in the Photosystem II antenna system of higher plants
pmc-12671495.creator: Zeno Guardini, Luca Dall’Osto, Rodrigo L Gomez, Roberto Caferri, Pierre Joliot, Roberto Bassi
pmc-12671495.description: Optimal photosynthetic performance of plants requires a balance between light energy capture and its use in downstream reactions. The process of light harvesting and its regulation are mediated by a complex array of antenna proteins, whose conservation throughout evolution suggests each complex serves a specific function in the diverse growth conditions in the natural subaerial environment.

pmc-12727576.title: Neutrophil extracellular trap markers predict thrombotic risk in patients with hyperhomocysteinemia: development and validation of a predictive model
pmc-12727576.creator: Lifan Shao, Shujie Zhang, Zhenyu Wang, Chang’an Pei, Yanjie Jiang, Guangxin Cao
pmc-12727576.description: BackgroundVenous thromboembolic diseases pose a serious threat to human health, and their pathogenesis is closely associated with the abnormal activation of neutrophils and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). However, the mechanisms underlying the role of NETs in thrombosis related to Hyperhomocysteinemia (hHcy) remain unclear.

pmc-12977092.title: Deep learning interpretability in neuroimaging: A comprehensive survey and methodological recommendations
pmc-12977092.creator: Md Mahfuzur Rahman, Vince Calhoun, Sergey Plis
pmc-12977092.description: Deep learning (DL) models have experienced a surge in popularity due to their capacity to directly learn from raw data in an end-to-end paradigm without relying on a separate feature extraction process that may be based on restrictive assumptions. The neuroimaging community has enthusiastically embraced DL as it strives to learn biomarkers from complex, multivariate, multimodal datasets.

pmc-13026878.title: Expanded Hemodialysis Using a Medium Cut-Off Dialyzer for Severe Valproic Acid Poisoning: A Case Report with Real-Time Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
pmc-13026878.creator: Celia Rodríguez Tudero, Avinash Chandu Nanwani, Elena Jiménez Mayor, Esperanza Moral Berrio, Marco Vaca Gallardo, Juan Daniel Díaz García, José C. De La Flor
pmc-13026878.description: Background: Valproic acid (VPA) poisoning has a dynamic clinical course and may require extracorporeal toxin removal (ECTR) in severe cases. Intermittent hemodialysis is the preferred ECTR technique; however, clinical experience with expanded hemodialysis (HDx) using medium cut-off (MCO) membranes in acute VPA intoxication is scarce.

pmc-13076901.title: Diagnosis model of early malignant pulmonary nodules based on clinical laboratory data
pmc-13076901.creator: Lisheng Liu, Hua Li, Yajun Miao, Weiwei Zhang
pmc-13076901.description: Accurate differentiation of malignant from benign pulmonary nodules remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning models integrating seven autoantibodies (7-AABs) and routine laboratory parameters for lung cancer risk prediction. We retrospectively enrolled 310 patients with pulmonary nodules (142 early-stage malignant, 168 benign). LASSO regression was used for feature selection.

pmc-13201695.title: Identification of glycometabolism-related genes for predicting the prognosis of patients with glioblastoma and its correlation with immune infiltration
pmc-13201695.creator: Xueshan Dong, Luhang Yu, Yifan Li
pmc-13201695.description: BackgroundAbnormal glucose metabolism has emerged as a prominent metabolic characteristic of various cancers, significantly influencing critical processes such as cell proliferation, metastasis, and invasion. Moreover, it plays an integral role in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment. Glioblastoma (GBM), recognized as the most prevalent malignant histopathology of the central nervous system (CNS), also exhibits notable abnormalities in glucose metabolism.
